sources.title: Climate Change Risk and Vulnerability Assessment: Trelawny
sources.organization: UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) and UNDP Jamaica, with the Green Climate Fund and Trelawny Municipal Corporation
sources.temporal_coverage: Report dated 10 August 2025; community risk and adaptive-capacity assessment with historical hazard records and projections through 2059.
sources.methodology: Parish CRVA combines hazard, exposure, sensitivity and adaptive-capacity indices, with stakeholder validation.
sources.limitations: The report notes gaps in localized data and long-term projections; recommendations are not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Change Risk and Vulnerability Assessment: Westmoreland
sources.organization: UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) and UNDP Jamaica, with the Green Climate Fund and Westmoreland Municipal Corporation
sources.temporal_coverage: Report dated 10 August 2025; historical hazard records and downscaled projections for 2030–2039, 2040–2049 and 2050–2059.
sources.methodology: Parish CRVA combines hazard, exposure, sensitivity and adaptive-capacity indices, with stakeholder validation.
sources.limitations: The report notes western-region projection gaps; options are proposals.

sources.title: Jamaica Systematic Country Diagnostic: Boosting Recovery and Sustainable Economic Growth
sources.temporal_coverage: Country diagnostic published in 2022, drawing on historical disaster, household, labor-market and social evidence available to the assessment.
sources.methodology: Country diagnostic synthesizes Jamaican economic, social, household and climate-risk evidence.
sources.limitations: Evidence largely predates 2022; no climate-caused violence finding.

sources.title: Jamaica's Progress Towards Implementation of Key Climate Change Adaptation Actions and Plans
sources.temporal_coverage: Performance audit of climate-adaptation planning and implementation during 2018/19–2024/25; selected project statuses are dated October 2025 or January 2026.
sources.methodology: Independent performance audit reviewed ministry records, project status, coordination, stakeholder engagement and monitoring.
sources.limitations: Findings describe the audit period and stated cut-off dates, not implementation status after January 2026.

sources.title: LG-ACT Project Brief
sources.organization: Ministry of Local Government and Community Development, Government of Jamaica
geographic_coverage: urban communities served by municipal water systems
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated government project brief; describes planned activities over a stated 27-month project period.
sources.methodology: Government project brief describes objectives, components and expected outcomes.
sources.limitations: The page gives no publication date or current status; expected outcomes do not demonstrate completed work.

sources.title: Parish Safety and Security Mechanism
sources.organization: Ministry of Local Government and Community Development, Government of Jamaica
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated government description of the parish-level safety and security mechanism.
sources.methodology: Ministry page describes committee mandates, participation and coordination functions.
sources.limitations: The page is undated and documents institutional design, not current operation or outcomes.

sources.title: Approach Paper: Jamaica Country Program Evaluation, Fiscal Years 2014–25
sources.organization: World Bank Group, Independent Evaluation Group
sources.temporal_coverage: December 2025 evaluation approach-paper context; not completed evaluation results.
sources.methodology: Evaluation approach paper synthesizing country context.
sources.limitations: Contextual diagnosis, not a completed impact evaluation or local causal estimate.

claims.paraphrase: Salt Marsh, Falmouth, Duncans, Troy, Wakefield, Bunkers Hill, Stettin, Wait-a-Bit, Ulster Spring and St. Vincent fall in Trelawny's highest composite-risk tier (moderate): very high sensitivity and low adaptive capacity elevate risk despite generally low hazard exposure.
claims.limitations: The composite tier is the highest within Trelawny, not a claim of the island's highest hazard exposure.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 7; adaptation priorities, PDF pp. 7–8.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies poor roads, limited health/education access, climate-sensitive farming and weak rural institutional presence as vulnerabilities; it recommends road, drainage, water, crop, mobile-health and preparedness measures for hotspot communities.
claims.limitations: These are report recommendations, not evidence that funding or implementation occurred.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF pp. 6–7; methodology, PDF pp. 11–12.
claims.paraphrase: Westmoreland's assessment projects warming, more erratic rainfall, drought, flooding and coastal surge risks; low-lying Negril and Savanna-la-Mar are named, while interior farming areas face water stress.
claims.scenario: The CRVA methodology uses downscaled RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 for 2030–2039, 2040–2049 and 2050–2059; the executive-summary warming range is not assigned to one pathway.
claims.limitations: The report notes local projection data gaps and scenario uncertainty; its 2050 summary range is not pathway-specific.

claims.paraphrase: Darliston, Enfield, Petersville and Belmont are identified as interior vulnerability hotspots with older populations, low incomes and poor service access; the report rates adaptive capacity as generally low, including in Savanna-la-Mar.
claims.limitations: Local composite assessment; no causal estimates.

claims.paraphrase: The CRVA proposes water harvesting and irrigation support in Darliston, Petersville and Broughton; gender-sensitive community training in Enfield and Whithorn; and drainage, resilient housing and mangrove protection in coastal towns.

claims.locator: Systematic Country Diagnostic, PDF p. 3, section 2.4.
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic reports overlapping climate/disaster risk, service and built-environment deficits, crime/violence, and social/economic exclusion in low-income often informal coastal settlements; women, youth, people with disabilities, fisherfolk and farmers are disproportionately affected.
claims.limitations: Co-location does not establish climate-caused violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The source reports overlapping climate and violence vulnerabilities, not climate-caused violence.

claims.locator: Systematic Country Diagnostic, PDF p. 3, section 2.4.
claims.paraphrase: It reports that weak land-use planning and limited services/jobs deepen spatial inequality and inner-city decay, raise crime and violence, and hamper economic activity; this increases vulnerability to climate shocks.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The diagnostic states that crime and violence hamper economic activity and increase climate-shock vulnerability.

claims.locator: Systematic Country Diagnostic, PDF pp. 56–57, climate vulnerability discussion.
claims.paraphrase: Female-headed households and children face disproportionate climate-shock impacts; rural poverty is more exposed where infrastructure is weaker and livelihoods depend on nature-based agriculture, while costly insurance and poor social-protection targeting constrain recovery.
claims.limitations: These are historical diagnostic findings, not a current post-Hurricane Melissa assessment.

claims.paraphrase: The audit's January 2026 status table still lists the Local Climate Adaptive Living Facility pilot as not started; its narrative says implementation had not begun by October 2025 while UNCDF–GCF grant-agreement clearance was pending.
institutions: Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation
claims.limitations: This is the audit's dated status through January 2026, not a current implementation update.

claims.paraphrase: For 2017–July 2024, the Climate Change Focal Point Network had no documented stand-alone meetings and one joint session; the Advisory Board met 14 of 32 expected times, weakening information exchange and coordination.
institutions: Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation
claims.limitations: These counts cover specified historical records; the report also records later corrective steps.

claims.paraphrase: The audit says engagement with youth and vulnerable groups was largely event-based; it also records a 2024 youth workshop with about 100 participants and six-location adaptation workshops with 137 participants.
claims.limitations: Reported events do not establish sustained representation in ongoing climate decision-making.

claims.paraphrase: The government brief proposes Westmoreland water governance: reliable rural potable water and urban drainage, rainwater storage and treatment, drought-period monitoring, community operator training, and participatory parish/community development committees.
institutions: Ministry of Local Government and Community Development
claims.limitations: The page is undated; planned components and expected outcomes are not evidence of completion.

claims.locator: Parish Safety and Security Mechanism, lines 44–49 and 75–86.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry describes mayor-chaired Parish Safety and Security Committees as local coordination and citizen-participation channels; the mandate lists natural disasters, exclusion of vulnerable groups and environmental risks among security and sustainability concerns.
institutions: Ministry of Local Government and Community Development
claims.limitations: The page is undated and does not demonstrate current committee operation or a climate-disaster-to-violence outcome.

search_audit.query: Jamaica parish climate change risk vulnerability assessment Trelawny Westmoreland named communities drought flood adaptive capacity
search_audit.outcome: Opened direct parish CRVA PDFs for Trelawny and Westmoreland; used named communities, livelihood and service gaps, and the reports' stated projection/data limitations.

search_audit.query: Jamaica climate shocks crime violence social exclusion coastal settlements women youth fisherfolk primary report climate security
search_audit.outcome: The 2022 World Bank diagnostic directly describes overlapping climate/disaster vulnerability, crime/violence and exclusion in poor coastal settlements; it does not say climate causes violence.

search_audit.query: Jamaica crime violence insecurity restrict climate adaptation access resilience climate shock vulnerability reverse pathway report
search_audit.outcome: The World Bank diagnostic states crime/violence hampers economic activity and increases climate-shock vulnerability; targeted searches found no verified named-community evidence that violence blocks climate adaptation access or that climate shocks trigger violence.

search_audit.query: Jamaica Westmoreland local adaptation water governance project climate capacity audit LoCAL municipal resilience
search_audit.outcome: Opened the government LG-ACT project brief, parish CRVAs and Auditor General performance audit; distinguished proposed capacity and consultation from verified implementation, and recorded the audit's dated LoCAL status.

gaps: The reviewed material supports co-location of climate/disaster vulnerability with crime, violence and exclusion, and an explicit reverse link from violence to climate vulnerability; it does not establish that climate shocks cause or escalate violence in Jamaica.
No directly inspected source established that insecurity prevents climate-adaptation access in a named community; the IEG approach paper's reverse link is national or generic-zone and not quantified.
The parish CRVAs provide named local assessments, but projections and composites carry stated data and scenario uncertainties; recommended actions are not proof of delivery.
The Auditor General's LoCAL status is dated through January 2026. The undated LG-ACT webpage does not establish present implementation or outcomes.

correction_audit.correction: Rebound from JAM-SRC-103 (2022 SCD) to newly verified JAM-SRC-107 (2025 IEG approach paper), exact paragraph 2.4. SCD remains source for JAM-C-108.
